name: Editorial Feature Rows
note: Each row declares a named view-timeline and its illustration is scrubbed by scroll: an @property percentage sweeps a highlighter across wrapped lines, graph edges draw via stroke-dashoffset, a sentence types out with steps(). Without animation-timeline support the same keyframes run on time once an IntersectionObserver sees the row.
html:
Marginalia Notes for people who read closely

Read closely. Think in links. Write with receipts.

01

Highlight once, find it forever

Mark a passage in any PDF, web page or e-book. Marginalia keeps the sentence, the page number and the reason you cared — searchable in the same box as your own writing.

  • 40 ms median search across 40,000 highlights
  • Imports from e-readers, browsers and scanned pages
02

Every note knows its neighbours

Type two square brackets and link anything to anything. The graph grows as you read, so the essay you start in March already knows what you underlined in September.

  • Backlinks update as you type, offline
  • Hover a note to trace what it touches
03

Cite without leaving the sentence

Start typing an author’s name and the passage you saved slides in with its page number. Footnotes, bibliography and quotation marks look after themselves.

  • Chicago, MLA and APA, switchable per draft
  • Every quote links back to its highlight

html:
Silverline for iPhone and Mac

Shoot digital. Develop like film.

01 / 05

  • ISO 1600 · fine grain
    01

    Grain that behaves like silver

    Clumps in the shadows, thins out in the highlights and changes every frame. Modelled on 40 scanned emulsions.

  • Halation
    02

    Halation around the highlights

    The red glow film gets when light bounces off the base. Dial it in per photo, from a whisper to a 1970s night shoot.

  • SensorDeveloped
    03

    See the difference, then commit

    Drag across the frame to compare the straight-from-sensor file with the developed one. Nothing is destructive.

  • Film stock+10 more
    04

    Fourteen stocks, profiled from real film

    Each one measured from a shot roll and a lab scan: colour response, contrast curve and how it falls apart when you push it.

  • 12 of 36 frames · developed in 4.2 s
    05

    Develop a whole roll at once

    Pick a stock, set the push, and Silverline matches exposure frame to frame. A 36-exposure roll takes about four seconds.
